title: Orchestrate hierarchical control-plane endpoint binding with staged DNS sync
author: Sophie Martin
description:
Motivation: Private control plane deployments must avoid DNS flapping and support staged rollouts when we change endpoint topology. Customers in multi-AZ and cross-account setups have asked for deterministic endpoint-to-subnet binding plus a safe, observable DNS rollout path that avoids simultaneous global switchovers. This PR introduces a hierarchical endpoint binding model (zone-primary / zone-secondary) and a staged DNS sync controller that applies Route53 Resolver rules and Route53 records in controlled waves.

What this PR does: 1) Terraform: adds a new module `controlplane-endpoint-group` that creates grouped ENIs, AZ affinity tags, and an ownership tag used by the installer to allocate endpoints deterministically. The module supports a `priority` attribute (primary|secondary) and optional healthcheck target. 2) Helm: introduces a new optional chart hook `staged-dns-controller` for the installer control-plane chart. The controller watches endpoint-group tags and orchestrates Route53/Resolver updates using a rollout policy. 3) Installer orchestration: the private-installer now computes a wiring plan during `terraform plan` -> `apply` and emits a `controlplane-wiring.json` artifact consumed by the Helm hook during upgrade. 4) Upgrade/rollback: rollout policies include wave-size, min-healthy-per-wave and a fast-abort path that reverts DNS in-flight if health thresholds fail. 5) Tests and docs: adds integration tests (local k8s + mocked Route53) and upgrade notes.

Backward compatibility and migration: The default behavior preserves existing single-endpoint-per-cluster semantics unless `enable_hierarchical_endpoints=true` is set. For customers who opt-in, we provide a migration plan: run `tf apply` with the module in dry-run to generate `controlplane-wiring.json`, then trigger a Helm release that applies staged DNS. Rollback is implemented by reversing the staged waves and optionally de-prioritizing endpoints via tags. No breaking change to existing state when feature flag is off.

Testing performed: - Unit tests for the Terraform module (validation for tag names, priority values). - Helm chart lint and integration test that spins up a KinD cluster and a route53-mock container. - End-to-end dry-run using a sandbox account with 3 AZs, 4 endpoints: simulated failure in wave 2 triggers fast-abort and restores previous records. - Load smoke tests to validate concurrent endpoint resolution behavior.

Operational notes: - The staged-dns-controller requires IAM permissions to modify Route53 records and Resolver rule associations; documented in INSTALLER_IAM.md. - Observability: controller emits metrics: dns_rollout_wave, dns_rollout_status, endpoint_health_gauge. - Rollout duration is proportional to wave_count; recommend wave_size >= 1 and wave_interval default 30s for low-risk rollouts.

Checklist: - [x] Terraform module with documentation and examples - [x] Helm hook and controller container image - [x] Integration tests and mock infra - [x] Upgrade/rollback scenarios validated - [x] Release notes and installer IAM updates

review_comments: Liang Chen: Please add a safety check so that the controller never writes a record with TTL < 30 — some customers rely on TTL semantics. Also can we add a metric for rollback_count?
Sophie Martin (author): Added TTL guard and rollback_count metric in images/staged-dns-controller/main.go; updated tests to assert TTL >= 30. See commit f7e0b11.
Asha Patel: IAM permissions look wide; please scope resolver association permissions to specific hosted zones when possible.
Sophie Martin: Narrowed IAM permissions in INSTALLER_IAM.md and added an example policy that limits to the account and hosted zone ARNs. See docs commit d2c7a6f.

Miguel Rivera: During upgrade where wave_size=1 this may take long for large clusters; we should document recommended wave_size and provide a CLI flag to override wave_interval. Could we also add a fast path for canary-only rollouts?
Sophie Martin: Added `--wave-interval` CLI flag and updated docs with recommended defaults; left canary-only path for a follow-up (tracked ENG-2332).

release_notes: Add hierarchical control-plane endpoint groups with AZ affinity and priority tagging (opt-in).
Introduce staged DNS rollout controller (helm hook) to apply Route53 changes in controlled waves.
Installer emits wiring artifact usable by rollout controller.
New IAM permissions required: Route53 record change and Resolver association actions. See INSTALLER_IAM.md.
